rows.citation: Van Geit W, Vanherpe L, Rössert C, et al. (2024). BluePyMM (v0.9.11). Zenodo / GitHub software release.
rows.model_type: biophysically detailed multi-compartment NEURON e-models (BluePyOpt) combined with many morphologies; not NeuroML
rows.controlled_mutations: no - varies morphology across e-model/morphology combinations from a circuit recipe; no recorded single-fault mutation operators.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - runs each e-model's full set of BluePyOpt fitness protocols per combination, but protocols are fixed inputs rather than a studied battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - scores every combination with the e-model's feature-based fitness calculator; eFEL is a listed dependency.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection or minimisation of protocols; configuration can only skip features and set per-feature thresholds.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - acceptance thresholds are set in configuration; no discovery/held-out model split or detection-rate evaluation.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI or code transformations considered.
rows.software: BluePyMM https://github.com/BlueBrain/BluePyMM (PyPI bluepymm 0.9.11; DataCite rights LGPL-3.0-only; GitHub API license NOASSERTION)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: BluePyMM gates whether an existing e-model generalises to new morphologies: a feature score passes if within a threshold scaled by the exemplar morphology's score. That reference-relative acceptance idea is close in spirit, but its targets are experimental feature scores, not a reference model's behaviour. NeuroSem would compare transformed vs reference models in NeuroML/LEMS with tolerances calibrated by numerical refinement, controlled single-fault mutants, greedy protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API api.github.com/repos/BlueBrain/BluePyMM (created 2017-05-04, pushed 2024-11-01); raw README.rst; source bluepymm/run_combos/calculate_scores.py and bluepymm/select_combos/table_processing.py (megate rule: score <= max(threshold, threshold x exemplar score)); PyPI JSON pypi.org/pypi/bluepymm/json; DataCite API api.datacite.org/dois/10.5281/zenodo.8146238 (authors, year 2024, v0.9.11, LGPL-3.0-only); README bibtex gives year 2023 for the same DOI (conflict noted, DataCite used); Zenodo API returned 504 twice; bluepymm.readthedocs.io overview page.

rows.citation: Tennøe S, Halnes G, Einevoll GT (2018). Uncertainpy: A Python Toolbox for Uncertainty Quantification and Sensitivity Analysis in Computational Neuroscience. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 12, 49. (Paper cited by the uncertainpy repository README.)
rows.model_type: model-agnostic black-box models, tailored to computational neuroscience (single-neuron voltage-trace models and spiking networks)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - perturbs parameters by sampling probability distributions (quasi-Monte Carlo, polynomial chaos); no discrete recorded mutation operators or structural edits.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - README and features docs retrieved do not describe multi-protocol batteries; the model is a user function that could encode any stimulus.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - feature-based: built-in SpikingFeatures and eFEL-based EfelFeatures for voltage traces, plus network spike-train features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no stimulus-protocol selection; the analysis targets parameter uncertainty and sensitivity.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no discovery/held-out split; it is an analysis toolbox rather than a detection-evaluation study.
rows.software: Uncertainpy https://github.com/simetenn/uncertainpy (GPL-3.0 per GitHub API; PyPI uncertainpy 1.2.3)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uncertainpy measures how feature outputs of one model vary with parameter distributions. NeuroSem instead asks whether one specific transformed model differs from its reference beyond calibrated numerical tolerance, across a stimulation battery, and selects protocols by detection of controlled mutants on held-out models. Uncertainpy could be a reuse point for choosing sensitivity-informed mutation magnitudes.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API api.github.com/repos/simetenn/uncertainpy (GPL-3.0, created 2015-04-23, pushed 2022-09-28); raw README.md (description, Citation section); PyPI JSON pypi.org/pypi/uncertainpy/json (1.2.3); uncertainpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/features.html; Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fninf.2018.00049 for the cited paper metadata.

rows.citation: Manninen T, Aćimović J, Havela R, et al. (2018). Challenges in Reproducibility, Replicability, and Comparability of Computational Models and Tools for Neuronal and Glial Networks, Cells, and Subcellular Structures. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 12, 20.
rows.model_type: neuronal and astrocyte signal-transduction (biochemical) models, spiking neuronal networks, and neurodevelopment simulation tools
rows.controlled_mutations: no - reimplements and re-simulates published models from their descriptions; no deliberate fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - compares models under their own published stimuli (e.g. glutamate stimulus vs spontaneous oscillation); no systematic current-clamp battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear - full text compares simulated dynamics across implementations; retrieved sections show no standardised single-cell electrophysiology feature extraction.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - review and case-study evaluation of tools and models; no held-out design.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: This review documents that reimplementations in other tools often fail to reproduce published behaviour, and it calls for built-in model validation. That motivates NeuroSem's translation/refactoring use-case, but the review offers no automated detection method. NeuroSem would operationalise such comparisons for NeuroML single-cell models with a mutation-calibrated, optimised, held-out-evaluated stimulation battery.

rows.citation: Raikov I, Close TG, Kumar S S, et al. (2013). Challenges of declarative modeling of conductance-based neurons in diverse simulation environments. BMC Neuroscience, 14(Suppl 1), P94.
rows.model_type: conductance-based neuron models (Purkinje, Golgi, cerebellar granule, CA1/CA3 pyramidal) ported to a prototype declarative language; single-compartment soma variants
rows.controlled_mutations: no - ports models across NEURON, NEST and GNU Octave; no deliberately injected faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - simulates current injection and voltage clamp in each environment; no systematic or varied protocol battery described.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - abstract quantifies differences between voltage and current traces directly; no feature-extraction method mentioned.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - one-page conference abstract without an evaluation design.
rows.ai_transformations: no - not considered; transformations are human code generation and porting.
rows.software: none (abstract mentions a prototype layer-oriented declarative language and a Python wrapper; no URL given)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: This abstract compares behaviour of the same conductance-based models after translation between simulators, which is close to NeuroSem's translation use-case. It reports only trace differences for a few models, with no method detail. NeuroSem would add feature-level comparison with numerically calibrated tolerances, controlled mutants, protocol selection and held-out evaluation within NeuroML/LEMS.

rows.citation: Diep M, Mekala RR, Ayyangar U, et al. (2021). Metamorphic Testing for Image-based Calcium Imaging Analysis Pipelines. 2021 IEEE/ACM 6th International Workshop on Metamorphic Testing (MET), pp. 53-60.
rows.model_type: neuroscience data-analysis software (CaImAn cell registration in a calcium-imaging pipeline); not neuron models
rows.controlled_mutations: no - applies metamorphic input transformations (rotation, translation, blurring, padding) to images; no program or model mutations.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - several input transformations are applied, loosely analogous to varied stimuli, but on imaging data.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - outputs compared are identified neuron cells from images.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of transformations or tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - feasibility study on one module.
rows.software: none released per abstract (tests CaImAn within the authors' BRAIN platform)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows metamorphic testing applied to neuroscience analysis software, not to simulation models. NeuroSem targets behavioural drift in neuron models themselves, using stimulation protocols, electrophysiology features, mutation-calibrated tolerances, protocol selection and held-out evaluation, none of which appear here.

rows.citation: Sinha A (2026). Building an AI Assistant for Computational Modelling with NeuroML. ankursinha.in (blog post, 30 January 2026).
rows.model_type: NeuroML model components generated or queried with LLM agents (general NeuroML)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no mutation or perturbation of models described.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - post describes no simulation-based behavioural checks of generated models.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - post reports no quantitative evaluation; model generation is described as work in progress.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - agentic LLM workflow iteratively generates NeuroML components checked by schema validation; generation of new models, not edits of existing ones.
rows.software: neuroml-ai (GitHub URL now redirects to NeuroML/neuroklea) https://github.com/NeuroML/neuroklea (GPL-3.0 per GitHub API; last push 2026-09-11)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows LLM-generated NeuroML exists and is checked structurally. NeuroSem would supply behavioural checks (multi-protocol feature comparison against a reference with calibrated tolerances) that could reveal drift invisible to schema validation. The current neuroklea MCP server lists model validation and sandboxed code execution, so whether it now simulates generated models is unverified.
